# Description For plain NVFP4 quantization with both row-wise and column-wise outputs, `NVFP4Quantizer::quantize_impl` computes the per-tensor amax into one buffer and then copies the four-byte scalar into the other with a separate `cudaMemcpyAsync`. This PR lets the amax reduction write the value to both buffers: the zeroing kernel clears both, and each thread block applies its atomic max to both. The device-to-device copy disappears, with no extra input read or kernel launch. Tested on an RTX 5050 (SM 12.0) against `main` built the same way (details under Validation): no test changes outcome, and a 1D or 2D quantize call issues one GPU operation fewer and takes 0.3 to 1.8 µs less (8.6% at 1024x1024). This is independent of #3749 (in-kernel NVFP4 scale swizzling on SM120/SM121); either can merge first. ## Type of change - [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content) - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Infra/Build change - [x] Code refactoring ## Changes - `current_scaling.cu`: `zero_amax_kernel` and `amax_kernel` take an optional second output. `compute_amax_impl` passes the column-wise amax as that output only for NVFP4 outputs whose column-wise amax is distinct from the buffer being reduced into; every other caller (FP8 current scaling, `compute_amax`, the 2D partial cast) keeps one output. - `quantizer.cpp`: remove the row-wise/column-wise amax copies from the non-RHT, non-row-scaled path. RHT post-transform amax and row-scaled per-row amax are untouched. - `recipe.h`: document that `nvte_compute_amax[_with_config]` fills both amax buffers of an NVFP4 output. - Test: `tests/pytorch/nvfp4/test_nvfp4_dual_amax.py` reuses one output tensor across inputs whose maximum decreases, reaches zero and rises again, and checks both amaxes against the input maximum for row-only, column-only and two-direction outputs, 1D and 2D quantization, BF16 and FP32 input, and aligned and tail shapes. The public API, scale computation and quantized values are unchanged. With a noop flag set, both buffers are now left untouched; previously the row-wise value was still copied into the column-wise buffer. # Validation `main` @ fac8d4a9 and this branch were built the same way (`NVTE_FRAMEWORK=pytorch NVTE_CUDA_ARCHS=120a NVTE_WITH_NCCL_EP=0 pip wheel . --no-build-isolation`, GCC 15.2, CUDA 13.4.92) and run on one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 (SM 12.0, 20 SMs, 8 GB, driver 615.71.10) with PyTorch 2.16.0.dev20261016+cu134 and Python 3.14.8. The NVFP4 directory and `test_numerics.py` ran with PyTorch's caching allocator capped at 6 GiB, releasing cached blocks between tests so that runtime-compiled kernels could still load (64 large-shape cases need more memory and fail with OOM on both builds). The other Python modules ran with a 2 GiB cap while another job shared the GPU. Counts come from the JUnit and gtest reports: on both builds most pytest processes, and some runs of the C++ test binary, exit with SIGSEGV after the last test, consistent with the exit-time crash that #3733 fixes. | | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---| | `pytest tests/pytorch/nvfp4` | 8,576 passed, 754 failed, 6,855 skipped | 8,600 passed, 754 failed, 6,855 skipped | | tests whose outcome changes | | none; the 24 added tests pass | | failures on both builds¹ | 754 | 754, identical messages | | new `test_nvfp4_dual_amax.py` | 24 passed² | 24 passed | | `pytest tests/pytorch/test_numerics.py -k nvfp4` | 137 passed, 106 skipped | 137 passed, 106 skipped | | `test_weight_swizzle_in_layers.py`; `test_torch_compile.py`, `test_quantized_tensor.py`, `test_fusible_ops.py` with `-k nvfp4` | 36, 47, 63, 257 passed | same tests pass | | C++ `test_cast_nvfp4_transpose`, `test_dequantize_nvfp4`, `test_swizzle`, `test_cast_current_scaling`, `test_cast_transpose_current_scaling` | 1,820 passed | 1,820 passed | | `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` over the 24 new tests, caching allocator off | | 0 errors | ¹ 530 in `test_nvfp4_group_quantize_graph_safe.py`, where the graph-safe grouped RHT cast kernel fails to launch on SM120 (`invalid argument`); 152 RHT reference comparisons in `test_nvfp4_group_quantize.py` and `test_nvfp4_rht_quantize_exact.py`; 64 OOM in `test_nvfp4_quantize_exact.py`; 8 SM120 swizzle-fusion expectations that #3749 addresses. ² `main`'s copy produces the same values, so the test passes there too (run with the 2 GiB cap). It guards the new path: the zeroing kernel must clear both buffers, or a later input with a smaller maximum leaves a stale column-wise amax. No new compiler warnings: the build emits the same warnings as `main`. `libtransformer_engine.so` for sm_120a grows by 200 bytes (170,060,488 to 170,060,688). What the `Lint` and `License` workflows run passes locally on this branch: `qa/L0_pytorch_lint` and `qa/L0_jax_lint` (cpplint 1.6.0, pylint 3.3.1, Python 3.12) and `qa/L0_license`. Beyond the sm_120a build above, `recipe/current_scaling.cu` compiles for the default architecture list (`75;80;89;90;100;120` with CUDA 13.4: sm_75, sm_80, sm_89, sm_90, sm_100, sm_120). ### GPU work per quantize call `torch.profiler` over one warm `q(x)` call, BF16 1024x1024 input, row-wise and column-wise output: | quantizer | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---| | 1D, 2D | `zero_amax_kernel`, `amax_kernel`, `Memcpy DtoD`, quantize (4) | `zero_amax_kernel`, `amax_kernel`, quantize (3) | | RHT | `ZeroAmaxKernel`, `HadamardAmaxTmaKernel`, quantize (3) | same (3) | With `optimize_for_gemm=True`, both builds add the two `swizzle_row_scaling_kernel` launches on SM120, so 1D and 2D go from 6 to 5 operations (#3749 removes those two launches for 128-aligned shapes). The same holds at 1088x1024. ### Time per quantize call `torch.utils.benchmark` `blocked_autorange` median of `q(x)`, the method of `benchmarks/benchmark_rht_cast_swizzle_fusion.py` extended to the 1D and 2D quantizers: BF16 input (`torch.randn`, seed 0), row-wise and column-wise output. The three builds alternated over two rounds of three measurements per cell with nothing else on the GPU; each value is the lowest of the six medians, and a cell's two round minima differ by at most 1.6 µs (5.7%). Times are host wall-clock per call, so at 1024x1024 they include each launch's host overhead. `optimize_for_gemm=False`: | quantizer | shape | `main` (µs) | this PR (µs) | change | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1D | 1024x1024 | 21.0 | 19.2 | -8.6% | | 1D | 2048x2048 | 28.9 | 28.6 | -1.0% | | 1D | 4096x4096 | 291.5 | 290.6 | -0.3% | | 1D | 8192x5120 | 725.2 | 724.3 | -0.1% | | 1D | 5120x8192 | 729.4 | 728.5 | -0.1% | | 2D | 1024x1024 | 20.9 | 19.1 | -8.5% | | 2D | 2048x2048 | 34.8 | 34.1 | -2.0% | | 2D | 4096x4096 | 295.7 | 294.8 | -0.3% | | 2D | 8192x5120 | 753.0 | 751.8 | -0.2% | | 2D | 5120x8192 | 783.2 | 782.4 | -0.1% | From 4096x4096 up, the saving is 0.8 to 1.2 µs (0.1% to 0.3%). With `optimize_for_gemm=True` it is 0.6 to 2.0 µs. Every 1D and 2D cell is faster on this branch, while RHT quantization, which this PR does not change, differs from `main` by at most 0.86 µs over its 15 cells.
bench_nvfp4_paths.py ```python """Per-call NVFP4 quantize time and GPU activity for the paths touched by the swizzle and amax PRs. Timing uses the method of benchmarks/benchmark_rht_cast_swizzle_fusion.py: torch.utils.benchmark blocked_autorange median of `q(x)` ("quant_only") and of `t = q(x); tex.swizzle_scales_for_gemm_(t)` ("quant_plus_swizzle", what te.Linear runs before the GEMM), BF16 input, rowwise+columnwise output, extended from RHT to the 1D and 2D quantizers. Each cell is measured `--repeats` times; the JSON keeps every median so a repeat contaminated by another process on the GPU stays visible. `--trace` instead records, with torch.profiler, the GPU kernels and memcpys of one warm call of each statement, so the removed swizzle kernel and amax copy can be checked directly. """ import argparse import json import time import torch import torch.utils.benchmark as benchmark import transformer_engine.pytorch as te # noqa: F401 import transformer_engine_torch as tex from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.nvfp4_tensor import NVFP4Quantizer STMTS = { "quant_only": "q(x)", "quant_plus_swizzle": "t = q(x); tex.swizzle_scales_for_gemm_(t)", } def make_quantizer(kind, optimize_for_gemm): q = NVFP4Quantizer( fp4_dtype=tex.DType.kFloat4E2M1, rowwise=True, columnwise=True, with_amax_reduction=False, amax_reduction_group=None, with_rht=kind == "rht", with_post_rht_amax=kind == "rht", with_random_sign_mask=kind == "rht", with_2d_quantization=kind == "2d", ) q.optimize_for_gemm = optimize_for_gemm return q def median_us(stmt, glb, min_run_time): t = benchmark.Timer(stmt=stmt, globals=glb, num_threads=1) return t.blocked_autorange(min_run_time=min_run_time).median * 1e6 def gpu_activity(stmt, glb): """Names of the GPU kernels and memcpy/memset operations of one call, in launch order.""" code = compile(stmt, "", "exec") exec(code, dict(glb)) # warm-up torch.cuda.synchronize() acts = [torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA] with torch.profiler.profile(activities=acts) as prof: exec(code, dict(glb)) torch.cuda.synchronize() events = [e for e in prof.events() if e.device_type == torch.autograd.DeviceType.CUDA] events.sort(key=lambda e: e.time_range.start) return [e.name for e in events] def main(): p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("--label", required=True) p.add_argument("--out", required=True) p.add_argument("--min-run-time", type=float, default=1.0) p.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3) p.add_argument("--kinds", default="1d,2d,rht") p.add_argument("--shapes", default="1024x1024,2048x2048,4096x4096,8192x5120,5120x8192") p.add_argument("--trace", action="store_true") args = p.parse_args() shapes = [tuple(int(v) for v in s.split("x")) for s in args.shapes.split(",")] rows = [] for kind in args.kinds.split(","): for shape in shapes: torch.manual_seed(0) x = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") for opt in (False, True): q = make_quantizer(kind, opt) y = q(x) # warm-up; also records which layout the call produced torch.cuda.synchronize() base = {"kind": kind, "shape": list(shape), "optimize_for_gemm": opt, "swizzled_after_call": bool(y._with_gemm_swizzled_scales), "allocated_swizzled": bool(q.make_empty(shape, dtype=x.dtype) ._with_gemm_swizzled_scales)} for name, stmt in STMTS.items(): glb = {"q": q, "x": x, "tex": tex} row = dict(base, stmt=name) if args.trace: row["gpu_activity"] = gpu_activity(stmt, glb) else: meds = [median_us(stmt, glb, args.min_run_time) for _ in range(args.repeats)] row.update(median_us=meds, best_median_us=min(meds)) row["time"] = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S") rows.append(row) print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) del x, y torch.cuda.empty_cache() with open(args.out, "w") as f: json.dump({"label": args.label, "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), "torch": torch.__version__, "trace": args.trace, "rows": rows}, f, indent=1) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
### Not covered - Only SM120 was run. The amax kernels are architecture-independent and the copy removal is in the common PyTorch path, so SM100/103/110 take the same code. - JAX does not call `nvte_compute_amax`. Other callers (FP8 current scaling, the NVFP4 2D partial cast) pass outputs without a distinct column-wise amax and keep one reduction output; the C++ current-scaling suites above cover that path. - No multi-GPU runs. With `with_amax_reduction`, the cross-rank MAX all-reduce still runs afterwards on both buffers, which hold the same local amax before it as they did with the copy. ### How to reproduce ```bash python -m pytest tests/pytorch/nvfp4/test_nvfp4_dual_amax.py # timing and kernel lists, once per build (script in the details block above) python bench_nvfp4_paths.py --label pr --out pr.json --kinds 1d,2d python bench_nvfp4_paths.py --label pr --out pr-trace.json --trace --shapes 1024x1024,1088x1024 ``` # Checklist: - [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst) - [x] The functionality is complete - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (the new tests pass; 754 existing NVFP4 tests fail on this SM120 GPU on `main` as well, see Validation) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable issues were found.

Summary

The PR writes the input maximum directly to both NVFP4 maximum buffers, removing a separate GPU copy. - NVFP4 quantization writes both distinct amax buffers during reduction.

Diagram

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Plain NVFP4 quantization] --> B[Select first maximum buffer] B --> C{Separate column-wise buffer?} C -->|Yes| D[Pass both buffers] C -->|No| E[Pass one buffer] D --> F[Clear selected buffers] E --> F F --> G[Reduce input maximum into selected buffers] G --> H[Quantize without a separate copy] ``` Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[Common, PyTorch\] Write both NVFP4 amax ..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/41e075b5001185e37e1817a3ffdac9fd7fa809fa) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

Thanks for creating the PR! I think the better solution for this is to create a single tensor for both amax_rowwise and amax_columnwise and let amax_columnwise alias to amax_rowwise when NVFP4 has a single amax. We can make that code change in quantizer.cpp

also records which layout the call produced torch.cuda.synchronize() base = {"kind": kind, "shape": list(shape), "optimize_for_gemm": opt, "swizzled_after_call": bool(y._with_gemm_swizzled_scales), "allocated_swizzled": bool(q.make_empty(shape, dtype=x.dtype) ._with_gemm_swizzled_scales)} for name, stmt in STMTS.items(): glb = {"q": q, "x": x, "tex": tex} row = dict(base, stmt=name) if args.trace: row["gpu_activity"] = gpu_activity(stmt, glb) else: meds = [median_us(stmt, glb, args.min_run_time) for _ in range(args.repeats)] row.update(median_us=meds, best_median_us=min(meds)) row["time"] = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S") rows.append(row) print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) del x, y torch.cuda.empty_cache() with open(args.out, "w") as f: json.dump({"label": args.label, "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), "torch": torch.__version__, "trace": args.trace, "rows": rows}, f, indent=1) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
### Not covered - Only SM120 was run. The amax kernels are architecture-independent and the copy removal is in the common PyTorch path, so SM100/103/110 take the same code. - JAX does not call `nvte_compute_amax`. Other callers (FP8 current scaling, the NVFP4 2D partial cast) pass outputs without a distinct column-wise amax and keep one reduction output; the C++ current-scaling suites above cover that path. - No multi-GPU runs. With `with_amax_reduction`, the cross-rank MAX all-reduce still runs afterwards on both buffers, which hold the same local amax before it as they did with the copy. ### How to reproduce ```bash python -m pytest tests/pytorch/nvfp4/test_nvfp4_dual_amax.py # timing and kernel lists, once per build (script in the details block above) python bench_nvfp4_paths.py --label pr --out pr.json --kinds 1d,2d python bench_nvfp4_paths.py --label pr --out pr-trace.json --trace --shapes 1024x1024,1088x1024 ``` # Checklist: - [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst) - [x] The functionality is complete - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes (the new tests pass; 754 existing NVFP4 tests fail on this SM120 GPU on `main` as well, see Validation) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@

+
+"""Check both NVFP4 amax outputs, including reuse with a decreasing maximum."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import transformer_engine.pytorch as te
+from transformer_engine.pytorch import NVFP4Quantizer
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ["row", "column", "both"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", [(128, 128), (160, 192)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_2d_quantization", [False, True])
+def test_nvfp4_amax_matches_input_after_reuse(direction, shape, dtype, with_2d_quantization):
+    """The second amax must reset and track the same input maximum as the first."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required")
+    available, reason = te.is_nvfp4_available(return_reason=True)
+    if not available:
+        pytest.skip(reason)
+    q = NVFP4Quantizer(
+        rowwise=direction != "column",
+        columnwise=direction != "row",
+        with_2d_quantization=with_2d_quantization,
+    )
+    q.optimize_for_gemm = False
+    out = q.make_empty(shape, dtype=dtype)
+    # The maximum decreases, reaches zero and rises again; stale atomic-max state fails.
+    for magnitude in (16.0, 0.5, 0.0, 2.0):
+        x = torch.full(shape, -magnitude, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+        q.update_quantized(x, out)
+        expected = x.float().abs().amax().reshape(1)
+        for name in ("_amax_rowwise", "_amax_columnwise"):
+            actual = getattr(out, name)
+            if actual is not None:
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable issues were found.

Summary

The PR writes the input maximum directly to both NVFP4 maximum buffers, removing a separate GPU copy. - NVFP4 quantization writes both distinct amax buffers during reduction.

Diagram

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Plain NVFP4 quantization] --> B[Select first maximum buffer] B --> C{Separate column-wise buffer?} C -->|Yes| D[Pass both buffers] C -->|No| E[Pass one buffer] D --> F[Clear selected buffers] E --> F F --> G[Reduce input maximum into selected buffers] G --> H[Quantize without a separate copy] ``` Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[Common, PyTorch\] Write both NVFP4 amax ..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/41e075b5001185e37e1817a3ffdac9fd7fa809fa) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

reviews.body: Thanks for creating the PR! I think the better solution for this is to create a single tensor for both amax_rowwise and amax_columnwise and let amax_columnwise alias to amax_rowwise when NVFP4 has a single amax. We can make that code change in quantizer.cpp
